messages:
alex: Quick share — ran cross-region multi‑GPU inference comparisons (SXM vs PCIe) for the t5-xxl int8 bring-up. Charts uploaded: https://drive.google.com/xxx. Observed ~18% higher median latency on PCIe nodes and a ~2.5x tail when we don’t pin NUMA. Any thoughts on what to dig into?

ops-bot: Job 4283 finished: perf-runner started by @alex. Artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1809456789/ (33 files) :white_check_mark:

maria: Can you paste the exact cmdline + kernel + allocator used? also which CUDA driver/cuBLAS/cuDNN versions?

alex: Sure — command we ran: 
```
./run_infer --model t5-int8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --gpus 4 --mode async --profile --out artifacts/
uname -a: Linux bench-aws-02 5.15.0-70-generic #77-Ubuntu SMP x86_64
CUDA: 11.7, cuBLAS: 11.10, cuDNN: 8.2
allocator: tcmalloc on host
```

kevin: From quick flamegraphs it looks like an allgather/host-copy spike on PCIe nodes (fallback path). NVLink/SXM nodes have much more even kernel time. Rough numbers I pulled: SXM median ~48ms, PCIe median ~57ms, PCIe p95 ~320ms, SXM p95 ~120ms.

sachin: That p95 gap usually points at cross-socket DMA + CPU scheduling jitter. Did you bind CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to physical GPU ids and pin host threads? If not, GPU kernels can be kicked from different NUMA nodes and memory ends up remote.

lisa: Quick sanity: run `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `numactl --hardware` on the node. Example snippet I often paste: 
```
# sample topo
GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3    CPU Affinity
GPU0    X      NV1     PCIe    PCIe    0-11
GPU1    NV1    X       PCIe    PCIe    12-23
```

alex: I did `numactl --hardware` earlier and saw allocations on remote node in the PCIe case. Re-running with `numactl --interleave=all` reduced p95 by ~30% but median barely moved. So pinning matters for tails.

kevin: For a stricter test try: `numactl --physcpubind=0-11 --membind=0 ./run_infer ...` per process (bind each process to local CPU range and memory). Also verify p2p: `nvidia-smi topo -p2p` and `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer` in a small program.

maria: Also measure NVLink bandwidth with `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvlink --status`. For int8 kernels, note which cuBLAS/cuDNN patch you're on — small driver changes can cause the runtime to pick a different int8 kernel or fallback to FP32.

alex: We're on cuBLAS 11.10/cuDNN 8.2. One clue: on PCIe nodes I see a lot of generic GEMM kernels instead of tensor-core int8 kernels — suggests the driver/runtime didn't select the int8 kernel for that shape (shape mismatch or unsupported). That would explain both higher latency and subtle quality diffs.

sachin: Yep — fallback to non-int8 matmul explains latency and weird logits. Two experiments: (1) try FP16 quant instead of int8 to see kernel parity, (2) try padding the KV cache shapes so the GEMM dims align to tensor-core-friendly multiples.

kevin: Another runtime knob: try `--kernel-launch-mode=cooperative` (our runtime has it) to reduce host->device launch overhead when NVLink isn't available — it helped eliminate some host-side spikes in similar infra.

lisa: Pasting small helper script I used to capture topo + numa: 
```
#!/bin/bash
nvidia-smi topo -m
numactl --hardware
lscpu | grep 'NUMA node'
```
Drop that next to your perf job and collect both before/after runs.

alex: Perfect — next steps: I'll re-run the PCIe nodes with strict NUMA pinning + P2P enabled and collect the new charts. If tails persist, we’ll try per-GPU kernel selection and a float16 quant sanity run. Will upload results to the same GDrive link. Thanks all :pray:
